title: India's Car Sales Just Hit an All-Time High. The Iran War Is the Reason People Are Buying CNG.
excerpt: Maruti Suzuki sold more cars in a single month than ever before. Its CNG bookings jumped 40 percent after four fuel price hikes in May.
body:
India's automakers sold more cars in May 2026 than in any previous month, defying four rounds of fuel price hikes that pushed petrol past ₹120 per litre in major cities. The numbers, reported on Monday, revealed a market adapting in real time to the economic fallout of the Iran war.

Maruti Rewrites the Record Book

Maruti Suzuki, which controls nearly half the Indian car market, reported domestic passenger vehicle sales of 190,337 units — a 40 percent jump over May 2025 and the highest monthly figure in the company's history. Total sales, including exports and commercial vehicles, reached 242,688 units.

The headline number masked a more interesting shift underneath. CNG vehicle bookings surged 40 percent as buyers scrambled for cheaper alternatives to petrol. Maruti sold a record 78,000 CNG vehicles in the month alone, a direct consequence of India raising fuel prices at least four times in May to offset losses from soaring crude costs linked to the Strait of Hormuz disruption.

"We had no choice but to pass on higher costs to customers," Partho Banerjee, Maruti's senior executive officer for marketing and sales, told reporters. The company announced price hikes of up to ₹30,000 across select models from June 2026.

Tata and Mahindra in a Dead Heat

Behind Maruti, the battle for second place was decided by just 1,069 units. Tata Motors held on with 59,090 units, a 42 percent year-on-year surge — the fastest growth rate among the top three. Mahindra and Mahindra sold 58,021 units, up 11 percent.

Hyundai came in fourth with 47,837 domestic units, a 9 percent increase but a 7.8 percent month-on-month decline from April. Toyota and Kia rounded out the top six with 30,574 and 27,586 units respectively.

The EV Breakthrough

The bigger story may be in electric vehicles. India's EV passenger vehicle market recorded its strongest month ever, with retail sales surging 80 percent year-on-year to 26,221 units. Tata crossed the 10,000-unit mark for the first time, selling 10,231 EVs — a 102 percent jump. Mahindra doubled its EV numbers to 6,133 units, outselling MG Motor for the third straight month.

The data showed a sharp acceleration in the second half of May, with 61 percent of all EV sales coming after the mid-month fuel price revisions. The war-driven fuel shock appears to be doing what years of government subsidies struggled to achieve: making Indians buy electric.

What It Means for NRIs

For the Indian diaspora watching the market, the numbers signal resilience. The top six automakers collectively sold 413,445 units, a 27 percent year-on-year increase. But the cost pressures are real. Maruti, Mahindra, Tata, and Hyundai have all raised prices from June. And the weak monsoon forecast threatens rural demand, which drives a significant share of entry-level car purchases.

What's Next

Maruti will unveil India's first flex-fuel passenger vehicle on June 4, a move tied to the government's push for ethanol blending. The company's exports rose 34 percent in May, though shipments to the Middle East slowed. Hyundai's exports fell 10 percent, reflecting the same regional disruption.

The auto sector enters June with momentum, but the war's shadow looms. If crude stays above $90 per barrel and fuel prices keep climbing, the CNG and EV shift could accelerate further — reshaping India's automotive landscape in ways that outlast the conflict.

Sources: Autocar India, Reuters, CarAndBike, Rushlane, Vahan registration data
author: Diaspora Desk
